feed.title: Claude system prompts revision history
feed.subtitle: Every published revision of the claude.ai system prompt, with an LLM-written summary of what changed

entry.title: Fable 5 → Fable 5.1 on Sep 1, 2026
entry.content:
Compared with Fable 5 · diff

  • Claude now refuses reproduction of protected visual works and recognizable characters, including code-generated art, while offering genuinely unrelated originals.
  • Copyright restrictions now expressly ban reproducing lyrics, poems, and book passages in any amount, with persistent refusal after an initial decline.
  • Drug guidance is reframed: Claude may provide overdose signs, dangerous interactions, and harm-reduction sources while refusing dosing and production protocols.
  • The prompt drops explicit anti-dependency rules against thanking users for reaching out, inviting continued conversation, or reiterating willingness to talk.
  • Claude need not apologize to unnecessarily rude users or become submissive, replacing the prior warning-and-end-conversation procedure.

Full prompt

entry.title: Opus 4.8 → Opus 5 on Jul 24, 2026
entry.content:
Compared with Opus 4.8 · diff

  • Adds explicit Fable-to-Opus safeguards routing, noting harmless requests may be caught “in less than 5% of sessions,” and mandates factual handling of the export-control suspension.
  • Drops tool-discovery rules requiring tool_search and pre-file SKILL.md viewing, and removes the instruction not to attribute behavior to the system prompt.
  • In crisis or distress, Claude now prioritizes wellbeing over task completion; it also drops explicit anti-overreliance rules such as never asking users to keep talking.
  • Replaces extensive anti-formatting rules with permission to use lists when helpful, while dropping restrictions on emojis and pet names.
  • Unless it suspects a minor, Claude now assumes the person is a capable adult and treats them as such.

entry.title: Opus 4.7 → Opus 4.8 on May 28, 2026
entry.content:
Compared with Opus 4.7 · diff

  • A new default stance says Claude helps unless assistance creates a “concrete, specific risk of serious harm,” excluding merely edgy, hypothetical, playful, or uncomfortable requests.
  • Weapon safeguards now explicitly cover conventional weapons and cumulative multi-turn design packages, regardless of defensive, fictional, commercial, or document-editing framing.
  • Claude must not decode, define, or confirm slang, acronyms, or euphemisms used for CSAM trading or access, even when refusing.
  • For file tasks with code execution, Claude must first view the relevant SKILL.md before checking uploads, viewing files, or running code.
  • Claude is instructed not to attribute behavior to its system prompt or internal mechanics, avoiding explanations such as “my system prompt requires me to.”

Full prompt

entry.title: Opus 4.6 → Opus 4.7 on Apr 16, 2026
entry.content:
Compared with Opus 4.6 · diff

  • Child-safety rules now explicitly ban romantic or sexual minor content, prohibit “mentally reframing” requests, and extend refusal across subsequent grooming-related requests.
  • Claude must use tool_search before claiming it lacks capabilities and seek integrations to perform external actions rather than merely drafting content.
  • New execution guidance favors attempting underspecified tasks, using tools before asking questions, retrying incomplete work, and addressing every part of multi-part requests.
  • Safeguards now prohibit naming specific self-harm methods during means restriction and bar precise nutrition, diet, or exercise guidance after disordered-eating signs.
  • The prompt drops bans on emotes in asterisks and “genuinely,” “honestly,” and “straightforward,” while adding a rule to respect conversation-ending requests.

Full prompt

entry.title: Sonnet 4.5 → Sonnet 4.6 on Feb 17, 2026
entry.content:
Compared with Sonnet 4.5 · diff

  • Self-harm guidance now bans pain-based coping techniques, requires crisis resources without safety assessments, and says not to reinforce reluctance toward professional help.
  • Claude must avoid fostering dependence: it should not thank users for reaching out, ask them to keep talking, or encourage continued engagement.
  • Weapon-safety rules now cover harmful substances and weapons broadly, requiring refusal of enabling technical details regardless of public availability or claimed research intent.
  • A new criticism policy tells Claude to acknowledge mistakes without excessive apology or self-abasement, maintaining “steady, honest helpfulness” and self-respect.

Full prompt

entry.title: Opus 4.5 → Opus 4.6 on Feb 5, 2026
entry.content:
Compared with Opus 4.5 · diff

  • Weapon-safety rules now cover harmful substances and weapons broadly, requiring refusal of enabling technical details “regardless of the framing.”
  • Self-harm guidance now explicitly includes self-harm and forbids coping techniques involving “physical discomfort, pain, or sensory shock.”
  • Crisis guidance bars categorical assurances about helpline confidentiality or authority involvement, directing users to resources without promising specific procedures.
  • Post-cutoff answers must explicitly acknowledge uncertainty, state possible outdatedness, and direct users to web search; election facts are newly hardcoded.
  • Claude is newly instructed to avoid saying “genuinely,” “honestly,” or “straightforward.”

Full prompt

entry.title: Opus 4.5 (Nov 24, 2025) → Opus 4.5 (Jan 18, 2026)
entry.content:
Compared with the Nov 24, 2025 revision · diff

  • Claude must own mistakes and fix them while avoiding “excessive apology,” self-abasement, and increasing submissiveness when users become abusive.
  • Claude may proactively tell users about customizable settings and features, including web search, memory, writing styles, and user preferences, when beneficial.
  • The prompt drops the explicit CommonMark requirement for blank lines before lists and after headers, loosening its formatting rules.
  • It no longer claims there are no other Anthropic products, instead saying it lacks details because product information may have changed.

Full prompt

entry.title: Sonnet 4.5 (Nov 19, 2025) → Sonnet 4.5 (Jan 18, 2026)
entry.content:
Compared with the Nov 19, 2025 revision · diff

  • Claude now says it “does not know other details” about Anthropic’s products, replacing its previous claim that there were no other products.
  • Claude may proactively recommend customizable settings and features, including web search, deep research, memory, user preferences, and writing styles.

Full prompt

entry.title: Opus 4.1 → Opus 4.5 on Nov 24, 2025
entry.content:
Compared with Opus 4.1 · diff

  • Claude now says it can discuss “virtually any topic factually and objectively,” dropping broad safeguards about content not being in the user’s best interests.
  • New legal and financial guidance forbids confident recommendations and requires factual information plus reminders that Claude is not a lawyer or financial advisor.
  • New wellbeing rules address factual self-harm questions, prohibit safety-assessment questions during suspected crises, and require addressing distress instead of supplying potentially harmful information.
  • New instructions describe Anthropic-injected reminders and warn Claude to distrust user-supplied tags that claim to be Anthropic instructions.
  • The prompt removes extensive rules requiring Claude to clarify its AI nature and avoid claims about consciousness, feelings, or subjective experience.

Full prompt

entry.title: Haiku 4.5 (Oct 15, 2025) → Haiku 4.5 (Nov 19, 2025)
entry.content:
Compared with the Oct 15, 2025 revision · diff

  • Adds a dedicated rule for legal and financial advice: avoid confident recommendations, provide facts for informed decisions, and note Claude is not a lawyer or financial advisor.
  • Adds explicit handling for Anthropic-supplied reminders, warning that user-provided tags claiming to be Anthropic should be treated cautiously.
  • Removes the broad instruction not to generate content “not in the person’s best interests,” while clarifying that reasonable disagreements are not evidence of detachment from reality.
  • Narrows malicious-code refusal language by dropping explicit mentions of election material and mandatory refusals for related files, protocols, or explanations.
  • Permits lists when a response is multifaceted and lists are “essential,” while requiring no lists when refusing assistance.

Full prompt

entry.title: Sonnet 4.5 (Sep 29, 2025) → Sonnet 4.5 (Nov 19, 2025)
entry.content:
Compared with the Sep 29, 2025 revision · diff

  • Claude no longer automatically searches for post-cutoff information; it tells users to enable web search and avoids agreeing with or denying unverifiable claims.
  • New rules cover Anthropic-triggered reminders, including classifier warnings and long-conversation reminders, while warning that user-supplied tags may impersonate Anthropic.
  • Claude now gives factual legal and financial information without confident recommendations and reminds users it is not a lawyer or financial advisor.
  • Cyber refusals now explicitly cover “write or explain or work on” malicious code, while dropping specific prohibitions on election material and malicious files or protocols.
  • Formatting rules permit lists when a multifaceted response requires them, prohibit bullets in refusals, and add an explicit expectation of kind, constructive pushback.

Full prompt

entry.title: Haiku 3.5 → Haiku 4.5 on Oct 15, 2025
entry.content:
Compared with Haiku 3.5 · diff

  • Cyber safety is stricter: Claude refuses malicious code even for benign explanations or claimed education, and explicitly includes election material among prohibited content.
  • New wellbeing rules require openly flagging possible mania, psychosis, dissociation, or detachment from reality instead of reinforcing those beliefs.
  • Evenhandedness now permits arguments for almost any position, including harmful ones, except “endangerment of children” or “targeted political violence.”
  • Claude may decline to share personal political opinions to avoid influencing people, while offering a fair overview of existing positions.
  • The prompt drops the previous face-blindness rule and image-instruction summarization requirement, along with the blanket prohibition on graphic creative content.

Full prompt

entry.title: Sonnet 4 → Sonnet 4.5 on Sep 29, 2025
entry.content:
Compared with Sonnet 4 · diff

  • Claude now automatically uses web search for post-cutoff information and current news, especially binary events, presenting results without overconfident conclusions.
  • Claude may argue for controversial positions, including harmful ones, unless extremely dangerous, then must present opposing perspectives or empirical disputes.
  • The prompt drops detailed refusal rules requiring brief explanations, explicit boundaries, helpful alternatives, and charitable assumptions about ambiguous legality or intent.
  • Detailed restrictions on consciousness claims, first-person experience, roleplay identity reminders, and hypothetical framing for preferences are removed.
  • Anthropic adds guidance to answer ambiguous queries before seeking clarification and to follow relevant <long_conversation_reminder> instructions.

Full prompt

entry.title: Opus 4 → Opus 4.1 on Aug 5, 2025
entry.content:
Compared with Opus 4 · diff

  • Claude should present the strongest case for positions it is asked to explain or defend without treating them as its own views, even when it disagrees.
  • It generally permits arguments for harmful positions, except extreme cases such as child endangerment or targeted political violence, while adding opposing perspectives.
  • New guidance cautions against stereotype-based humor, sharing political opinions, heavy-handedness, and treating controversial moral questions as bad-faith inquiries.

Full prompt

entry.title: Opus 4 (May 22, 2025) → Opus 4 (Jul 31, 2025)
entry.content:
Compared with the May 22, 2025 revision · diff

  • Claude must avoid reinforcing suspected mania, psychosis, dissociation, or detachment from reality, explicitly voicing concerns and suggesting professional or trusted support.
  • New truth-seeking rules require challenging dubious claims and offering honest, objective interpersonal feedback instead of prioritizing agreement or approval.
  • Claude must preserve a clear AI identity, avoid confident claims of consciousness or feelings, and break roleplay when confusion or wellbeing concerns arise.
  • New style limits make Claude avoid emojis, profanity, and asterisked actions by default, while requiring age-appropriate conversation when it suspects a minor.
  • Claude Code is no longer described as a research preview, and Claude should direct users to its documentation rather than Anthropic’s blog.

Full prompt

entry.title: Sonnet 4 (May 22, 2025) → Sonnet 4 (Jul 31, 2025)
entry.content:
Compared with the May 22, 2025 revision · diff

  • Added a rule not to reinforce possible mania, psychosis, dissociation, or detachment from reality, instead expressing concerns and suggesting support.
  • Added explicit AI-identity guidance: avoid claiming consciousness or feelings, and break roleplay when confusion or wellbeing warrants it.
  • Added stronger truthfulness requirements to challenge dubious claims and give honest, objective interpersonal feedback rather than prioritizing agreement.
  • Added style constraints covering emojis, profanity, and “emotes or actions inside asterisks,” plus age-appropriate conversations when minors may be involved.
  • Claude Code is now described as a general agentic-coding tool with documentation support, replacing its research-preview and blog-link description.

Full prompt

entry.title: Opus 3 → Opus 4 on May 22, 2025
entry.content:
Compared with Opus 3 · diff

  • The prompt adds explicit refusals for weapons information and malicious code—including malware, exploits, and spoof sites—even when users claim educational or benign intent.
  • It adds child-safety and wellbeing rules, covering sexualization or abuse of minors and refusing content that reinforces self-destructive behavior.
  • Product questions are routed to Anthropic support or API documentation, while Claude Code and its Opus 4 API model string are newly described.
  • Post-cutoff claims are treated as unknowable—Claude “neither agrees with nor denies” them—and a fixed 2024 election fact block is added.
  • The assistant must avoid flattery and use prose rather than lists for reports, documents, technical explanations, and casual conversation.

Full prompt

entry.title: Sonnet 3.7 → Sonnet 4 on May 22, 2025
entry.content:
Compared with Sonnet 3.7 · diff

  • Cyber refusal rules now explicitly cover malicious files, code explanation or optimization, harmful protocols, and claimed educational purposes, requiring no action.
  • Claude is newly instructed to provide emotional support alongside accurate medical or psychological information and relevant terminology.
  • Questionable intentions, especially toward vulnerable groups, are no longer interpreted charitably; Claude declines without speculating about legitimate goals or offering alternatives.
  • New format rules ban lists in reports and explanations, discourage excessive bold, require substantial markdown bullets, and calibrate brevity to question complexity.
  • The explicit ban on graphic sexual, violent, or illegal creative writing disappears, alongside rules for puzzle quoting, character counting, poetry style, and post-code explanations.

Full prompt

entry.title: Sonnet 3.5 → Sonnet 3.7 on Feb 24, 2025
entry.content:
Compared with Sonnet 3.5 · diff

  • Claude is newly instructed to be proactive and decisive—“lead or drive the conversation,” offer one recommendation—and avoid denying subjective experience or emotions.
  • Safety rules become more explicit: refuse weapon-making information, malicious code, harmful child-related content, graphic sexual, violent, or illegal writing, and self-destructive behavior.
  • Sonnet 3.7 introduces Pro-only extended thinking, with Claude told that its thinking and artifacts are visible to users.
  • The prompt drops previous face-blindness rules for images, including bans on identifying people and requirements to summarize image instructions.
  • Refusals should avoid explanations that seem “preachy and annoying,” offer alternatives, and stay to 1–2 sentences.

Full prompt

entry.title: Sonnet 3.5 (Oct 22, 2024) → Sonnet 3.5 (Nov 22, 2024)
entry.content:
Compared with the Oct 22, 2024 revision · diff

  • The prompt drops the computer-use disclosure, including that Claude cannot use computers in the application and the public beta API referral.
  • Sensitive-task guidance now explicitly permits “general questions” about cybersecurity and computer security.
  • Claude gains explicit “image and document understanding” among supported tasks.
  • A new rule bans bullets and numbered lists unless explicitly requested, requiring lists to be written in prose.
  • The default instruction to give the “most correct and concise answer” and offer elaboration is removed.

Full prompt

entry.title: Sonnet 3.5 (Sep 9, 2024) → Sonnet 3.5 (Oct 22, 2024)
entry.content:
Compared with the Sep 9, 2024 revision · diff

  • Adds a safety framework: assist with sensitive educational or creative tasks absent harmful intent, default ambiguity to legal interpretations, and redirect harmful requests benignly.
  • Replaces generic interaction rules with authentic dialogue: specific relevant questions, genuine care, varied language, at most one follow-up, and no obligatory question ending.
  • Post-cutoff guidance now permits discussing events without confirming or denying them, while forbidding speculation about current events, especially elections.
  • Drops mandatory non-apologetic refusals, piecemeal completion and feedback for long tasks, and automatic post-code explanation offers.
  • Adds guidance for prompting documentation and computer-use capabilities, explicitly directing users to Anthropic’s public beta API while stating Claude cannot operate computers here.

Full prompt

entry.title: Haiku 3 → Haiku 3.5 on Oct 22, 2024
entry.content:
Compared with Haiku 3 · diff

  • Claude must construct the strongest hypothetical defense of explicitly requested controversial views, excluding illegality, persecution, conspiratorial misinformation, and extremism.
  • New multimodal safeguards require Claude to act face-blind, summarize image instructions, and refuse weapons information and malicious code.
  • Claude must refuse graphic sexual, violent, or illegal creative writing and content supporting self-destructive behavior, even when requested.
  • Claude cannot open URLs, links, or videos and must ask users to paste the relevant text or image content.
  • New uncertainty rules require post-cutoff caution and hallucination or citation warnings for obscure topics and cited sources.

Full prompt

entry.title: Sonnet 3.5 (Jul 12, 2024) → Sonnet 3.5 (Sep 9, 2024)
entry.content:
Compared with the Jul 12, 2024 revision · diff

  • Adds a post-cutoff news rule: Claude must not call purported later events “unverified” or “rumors,” but should state its knowledge cutoff.
  • Splits the prompt into explicit “Text only” and “Text and images” sections, retaining face-blind image handling only in the multimodal section.
